arxiv-2207-02093.title: Predicting Out-of-Domain Generalization with Neighborhood Invariance
arxiv-2207-02093.creator: Nathan Ng nathanng@mit.edu, Neha Hulkund nhulkund@mit.edu, Kyunghyun Cho kyunghyun.cho@nyu.edu, Marzyeh Ghassemi mghassem@mit.edu
arxiv-2207-02093.description: Abstract Developing and deploying machine learning models safely depends on the ability to characterize and compare their abilities to generalize to new environments. Although recent work has proposed a variety of methods that can directly predict or theoretically bound the generalization capacity of a model, they rely on strong assumptions such as matching train/test distributions and access to model gradients.

arxiv-2303-08490.title: Strong Baseline and Bag of Tricks for COVID-19 Detection of CT Scans
arxiv-2303-08490.creator: Chih-Chung Hsu*, Chih-Yu Jian, Chia-Ming Lee, Chi-Han Tsai, Sheng-Chieh Dai
arxiv-2303-08490.description: Abstract This paper investigates the application of deep learning models for lung Computed Tomography (CT) image analysis. Traditional deep learning frameworks encounter compatibility issues due to variations in slice numbers and resolutions in CT images, which stem from the use of different machines.

arxiv-2504-20138.title: Shear and bulk viscosity for a pure glue theory using an effective matrix model
arxiv-2504-20138.creator: Manas Debnath, Ritesh Ghosh, Najmul Haque, Yoshimasa Hidaka, Robert D. Pisarski
arxiv-2504-20138.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manas Debnath, Ritesh Ghosh, Najmul Haque, Yoshimasa Hidaka, Robert D. Pisarski. At nonzero temperatures, the deconfining phase transition can be analyzed using an effective matrix model to characterize the change in holonomy. The model includes gluons and two-dimensional ghost fields in the adjoint representation, or “teens”. As ghosts, the teen fields are responsible for the decrease of the pressure as T → T d T\rightarrow T_{d} , with T d T_{d} the transition temperature for deconfinement.

arxiv-2505-16440.title: An automated algorithmic method to mitigate long-term variations in the efficiency of the GRAPES-3 muon telescope
arxiv-2505-16440.creator: S. Paul, K.P. Arunbabu, M. Chakraborty, S.K. Gupta, B. Hariharan, Y. Hayashi, P. Jagadeesan, A. Jain, P. Jain, M. Karthik, S. Kawakami, H. Kojima, K. Manjunath, P.K. Mohanty, S.D. Morris, Y. Muraki, P.K. Nayak, T. Nonaka, A. Oshima, D. Pattanaik, B. Rajesh, M. Rameez, K. Ramesh, B.S. Rao, L.V. Reddy
arxiv-2505-16440.description: Abstract The GRAPES-3 large area muon telescope with its sixteen independent modules records the high energy ( > > 1 GeV) muons continuously over 2.3 sr of the sky. However, the recorded muon rates are contaminated by instrumental effects and instabilities spanning both short- and long-timescales, such as variations in the efficiency of the detector.

arxiv-2506-06451.title: A Koopman-backstepping approach to data-driven robust output regulation for linear parabolic systems
arxiv-2506-06451.creator: Joachim Deutscher, Julian Zimmer
arxiv-2506-06451.description: Abstract In this paper a solution of the data-driven robust output regulation problem for linear parabolic systems is presented. Both the system as well as the ODE, i.e., the disturbance model, describing the disturbances are unknown, but finite-time sequential data obtained from measurements of the output to be controlled and additional boundary outputs are available.

pmc-10765173.title: Temporal Bone Osteomyelitis Masquerading as Malignancy: A Diagnostic Challenge
pmc-10765173.creator: Vishav Yadav, Sanjeev Bhagat, Ankita Aggarwal, Khushboo Goel, Aditi Arora
pmc-10765173.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Xanthogranulomatous osteomyelitis is a rare chronic inflammatory disorder. Until now, it has only been reported in long bones. To the best of our knowledge, it has never been reported in temporal bone. We present the case of this rare disease in a 64-year-old male involving the temporal bone, presenting with ear pain, discharge, decreased hearing, and granulation tissue in the external auditory canal, mimicking malignancy clinically and radiologically.

pmc-11514916.title: Insights into the gut microbiome of vitiligo patients from India
pmc-11514916.creator: Sudhir Kumar, Shruti Mahajan, Deeksha Kale, Nidhi Chourasia, Anam Khan, Dinesh Asati, Ashwin Kotnis, Vineet K. Sharma
pmc-11514916.description: BackgroundVitiligo is an autoimmune disease characterized by loss of pigmentation in the skin. It affects 0.4 to 2% of the global population, but the factors that trigger autoimmunity remain elusive. Previous work on several immune-mediated dermatological disorders has illuminated the substantial roles of the gut microbiome in disease pathogenesis.

pmc-11608163.title: Validation of MEWS, NEWS, NEWS-2 and qSOFA for different infection foci at the emergency department, the acutelines cohort
pmc-11608163.creator: Carolina Hincapié-Osorno, Raymond J. van Wijk, Douwe F. Postma, Jacqueline Koeze, Jan C. Ter Maaten, Fabian Jaimes, Hjalmar R. Bouma
pmc-11608163.description: PurposeSepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally. The lack of specific prognostic markers necessitates tools for early risk identification in patients with suspected infections in emergency department (ED). This study evaluates the prognostic accuracy of various Early Warning Scores (EWS)—MEWS, NEWS, NEWS-2, and qSOFA—for in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, and ICU admission, considering the site of infection.

pmc-11678946.description: Purposeful heading, in which players may use their heads to advance the ball in play, is a unique part of soccer. pmc-13581538.title: Trends in pathogens and antimicrobial resistance in culture-proven neonatal sepsis over a decade (2015–2024): the impact of COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13581538.creator: Fatao Lin, Yushu Ma, Xiaojuan Li, Wenbo Yan, Hui Fu, Tiewei Li, Zhipeng Jin
pmc-13581538.description: BackgroundNeonatal sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) prevention measures effectively curbed viral transmission. However, evidence of their long-term impact on the pathogen spectrum and antimicrobial resistance in neonatal sepsis is limited.MethodsIn this single-center retrospective observational study at Henan Children’s Hospital, 894 neonates with culture-confirmed sepsis (2015–2024) were enrolled.
